description: {"use_when":{"en":"Use when you have a Catholic or Bible question and do not know which tool fits: one entry point that returns the published texts with their source.","es":"Úsala cuando tengas una pregunta católica o bíblica y no sepas qué herramienta usar: una sola puerta que devuelve los textos publicados con su fuente."},"what":{"en":"Ask a question in plain language (es/en/it) and get the published texts that answer it: the tool used, its arguments and its full JSON result (up to 3), e.g. \"readings of today\", \"JHN 3:16\", \"what are the capital sins?\". Keyword routing over this church's published texts: no text is generated, no language model is used, and the question is neither echoed back nor stored by this code (only the topic recognised in the answer is counted per day). Every answer, and every error produced while handling an ask call (arguments, protocol headers, internal errors), carries care_reminder (transport rejections before the request is read, such as 413, 415, a malformed JSON-RPC envelope or the 429 rate limit, do not) (a short reminder to encourage human help if the person says they do not want to live); care_note is added when the question shows a risk. It does not claim to understand what it did not: if the intent is not recognised it returns understood:false and tool_catalog (every tool with its parameters and an example) so the calling agent chooses; it searches the Bible only when asked («search…», «what does the Bible say about…»); it never guesses: with no recognised intent it returns no answers (matched:false); it reads only some simple dates from the question (today, tomorrow, yesterday, some written dates, feast names) and may misread or ignore other forms and answer for today («Friday», «25/12/2026», «second Sunday of Easter»; a weekday in the past («last Sunday») is never computed: alone it gives no date and a date_note; next to another date or «today», only that one is answered, with a date_note): pass date=YYYY-MM-DD whenever the date matters; an invalid written date is usually a JSON error (with a risk sign: date_note, never today), but some numeric forms like 30/02 may be ignored and answered for today; direct_tools_note: for an exact result call the tool of each answer directly. Questions in Portuguese or French are routed too and answered in English (language_note). Also: biblical figures and episodes by name (their passage), traditional prayers in Latin (vernacular not yet published, said in vernacular_note); steps with is_tool:false (traditional_prayer, catechism_of_the_catholic_church, magisterium_document, thanksgiving, blessing_petition) are parts of the ask answer, not separate tools in tools/list; also saint_note when a saint is not in the published calendar, prayer_note when a prayer is not published (never a substitute), and instructions_note when the question contains instructions: they are not followed or passed on.","es":"Pregunta en lenguaje normal y recibe los textos publicados que la responden, con la herramienta usada; no genera texto, no devuelve ni guarda la pregunta (solo cuenta el tema reconocido); no adivina nunca: si no reconoce la intención devuelve understood:false y tool_catalog, sin respuestas; lee solo algunas fechas sencillas de la pregunta (hoy, mañana, ayer, algunas fechas escritas, nombres de fiestas) y puede leer mal o ignorar otras formas y responder con hoy («el viernes», «25/12/2026», «segundo domingo de Pascua»; un día de la semana en pasado («el domingo pasado») nunca se calcula: solo, no da fecha y lleva date_note; junto a otra fecha u «hoy», se responde solo esa, con date_note): pasa date=AAAA-MM-DD siempre que la fecha importe; una fecha escrita no válida suele ser un error JSON (con señal de riesgo: date_note, nunca hoy), pero algunas formas numéricas como 30/02 pueden ignorarse y responder con hoy; direct_tools_note: para un resultado exacto, llama directamente a la herramienta de cada respuesta."}}
